**Finding submitted — T4C: deviation.**

- **Term/termination landscape:** § 11.1 sets a five-year initial term with one-year auto-renewals (30 days' non-renewal notice — a RENEWAL mechanic, not a convenience right). § 11.2 allows termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. Other termination hooks (§ 3 acceptance failure, § 7 warranty, § 8 indemnity) are all cause-based. Exhibit B / Payment Terms contain no early-termination fee or acceleration.
- **Why it fails fallback:** Corio has no convenience exit at all in a multi-year committed term — walk-away territory, not a minor wording gap.
- **Cure (preferred, shortest complete):** one inserted § 11.2A giving Corio a 30-day convenience termination with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; fallback of 60–90 days offered in the comment.
- **Already met:** Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right, since § 11.2 confines its termination to breach and insolvency — so nothing was added on that element, and the non-renewal notice was not double-flagged.
